name: Pleasant Mountain Lookout Tower
summary: Oxford County, ME steel fire tower on Pleasant Mountain, erected 1920 at 48 ft in Denmark; standing, now described as boarded up.
design: Steel lookout tower, 48 ft in 1920; glass-enclosed cab at the summit (Secret Falls trail page)
agency: Maine Forest Commissioner (1920 report); Maine Forest Service (1922 map and current signage per Press Herald)

access.note: Summit trails are open for four-season hiking (Press Herald); the tower is described as boarded up, so climbing it is not confirmed

visit.trail_note: Ledges Trail, 1.8 miles, the shortest and most popular route up the eastern side; trail network managed by Loon Echo Land Trust

events.note: Forest Commissioner's construction crew erected a 48-ft steel tower in the town of Denmark, with a camp and over three miles of telephone line
Maine Forest Service 360-degree panoramic map centered on the Pleasant Mt. fire tower in Denmark
Bath Independent (Aug 17, 1939): the fire tower at the summit is manned through the summer season
Bridgton News (July 9, 1943) reports a Portland paper's announcement that an observation post is to be established near the fire tower, with a chief observer from Denmark; opening not confirmed
